newsitem.title: FINLAND: Metra eyes Sulzer ship engines - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Metra eyes Sulzer ship engines - CEO.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Metra Oy Ab seeks cooperation with Swiss diesel engine maker New Sulzer Diesel to strengthen its Wartsila Diesel unit's position in marine engines, Metra CEO Georg Ehrnrooth said on Tuesday.
"Cooperation would broaden our product range to cover all kinds of marine engines," Ehrnrooth told Reuters.
Asked whether recently announced talks with Italian Fincantieri could lead to an acquisition or cross-ownership, Ehrnrooth said: "Metra does not rule out any option".

"Wartsila Diesel is the world's leading manufacturer of medium-speed diesel engines. Sulzer is one of the two leading manufacturers of low-speed engines," he said, adding Sulzer is particularly well-known for its big ocean ship engines.
Ehrnrooth declined to give any details about the talks or the schedule.
Fincantieri holds 50 percent of New Sulzer Diesel and has an agreement to buy the rest from Vulcan Industrie Holding GmbH, which is controlled by the bankruptcy estate of Bremer Vulcan Verbund AG.
Metra last Friday announced it had started talks about possible cooperation between Wartsila Diesel and Sulzer.
In 1995, Sulzer's net sales were 672 million Swiss francs. Wartsila Diesel, Metra's biggest business group, last year reported net sales of 6.9 billion markka.
